title: Protocol Routing
desc: Share one port between several services: connections are identified by protocol and sent to different backends, TLS by SNI and ALPN, HTTP by Host, without decryption
moduleOffTitle: The protocol routing module is disabled
empty: No rules yet. Add a rule to let several services share port 443 or another port
listenAddressPlaceholder: Leave empty to listen on all addresses
targetPortsPlaceholder: Leave empty to match the listen ports; the counts must match, or enter just one
savedRestarted: Saved. Rules restarted with the new settings
proxyProtocolHelp: TCP only. Sends a PROXY protocol header after connecting to the target so the downstream learns the real client address (haproxy accept-proxy, nginx proxy_protocol, or "Accept PROXY protocol" in Gately Web Services). Connections fail if the target does not support it.
routeDomainsPlaceholder: SNI domains, one per line: vpn.example.com, *.example.com or *. Leave empty to match every TLS connection
routeHostsPlaceholder: Host domains, one per line: files.example.com, *.example.com or *. Leave empty to match every HTTP connection
routeAlpnPlaceholder: ALPN (optional, comma-separated): h2, http/1.1, acme-tls/1. Leave empty for any
defaultTargetPlaceholder: Used when no route matches or the protocol is not recognized. Leave empty to drop the connection
defaultTargetNone: Not set, unmatched connections are dropped ({rejected} dropped)
sniffTimeoutHelp: One decimal place allowed; 0 means the default of 5 seconds. A client that sends nothing within this time goes to the Wait timeout route (or the default target if there is none), so this is also how long VNC and similar connections wait. TLS, SSH, HTTP and similar clients send their first packet within milliseconds of the handshake, so 0.3–1 seconds is recommended when there is a Wait timeout route
protocolHelp: TCP only; tcp is dual-stack IPv4+IPv6, tcp4 and tcp6 limit it to one address family
moduleEnabled: The protocol routing module is enabled
noRoutes: No routes; every connection goes to the default target
filterPlaceholder: Search name, group, port, target, domain or protocol
routesHelp: TLS, HTTP and Minecraft routes match by domain: exact domains first, then the longest *. wildcard, then *, then routes without domains. Case-insensitive. Under the same domain, TLS routes with ALPN take precedence. Other protocols allow one route each. An empty target port means the same as the listening port. PROXY protocol is set per route

protoHelp.tls: ALPN narrows a route down by application protocol, e.g. acme-tls/1 (TLS-ALPN-01 certificate validation) or postgresql (PostgreSQL 17 direct TLS connections)
protoHelp.http: Plain HTTP, including HTTP proxy requests (CONNECT), WebDAV and HTTP/2 with prior knowledge (h2c carries no Host and only matches routes without domains)
protoHelp.openvpn: OpenVPN in TCP mode, with tls-auth, tls-crypt and tls-crypt-v2
protoHelp.postgresql: Covers plain connections and the SSLRequest sent first with sslmode=prefer/require
protoHelp.timeout: For protocols where the server sends first, such as VNC, MySQL, FTP, SMTP, POP3 and IMAP. Their clients send nothing after connecting, so their traffic looks the same: pick one per port. Connections are forwarded once the detection timeout expires; 0.3–1 seconds works well
protoHelp.minecraft: Routed by the server address in the handshake, so servers for several domains can share one port like SNI routing; data appended to the address by Forge, BungeeCord or TCPShield is ignored, and the server list ping of 1.6 and earlier carries no address
protoHelp.rtsp: Request line version RTSP/1.0 or RTSP/2.0, as used by IP cameras and NVRs
protoHelp.sip: Plain SIP over TCP; use a TLS route for SIP over TLS
protoHelp.redis: Clients that send commands as RESP arrays (redis-cli and client libraries); use a TLS route for Redis with TLS
protoHelp.amqp: AMQP 0-9-1 (RabbitMQ) and AMQP 1.0; use a TLS route for AMQPS
protoHelp.smb: SMB1, SMB2 and SMB3 directly over TCP
protoHelp.git: The git:// protocol served by git daemon; Git over HTTPS or SSH uses the TLS, HTTP or SSH routes
protoHelp.bittorrent: Peer connections without protocol encryption; encrypted (MSE) connections have no signature and go to the default target
protoHelp.adb: Plain adb connect sessions; wireless debugging since Android 11 uses TLS
protoHelp.irc: Plain IRC clients (they send CAP, PASS, NICK or USER first); use a TLS route for IRC over TLS

routeMinecraftPlaceholder: Server addresses, one per line: mc.example.com, *.example.com or *. Leave empty to match every Minecraft connection
